theory.text: Match sentence beginnings with endings to form statements supported by the passage. Grammar can help eliminate choices, but evidence and meaning determine the answer.
Key skills: Recognising purpose, cause, sequence and paraphrased ideas.

guide.text: Read the beginnings  predict a meaningful continuation  find the supporting evidence  compare the endings  ensure that every completed statement is accurate.

small.text: Text: “As batteries improved, electric buses could travel longer distances between charges.”
Improved batteries allowed buses to ... A. travel farther. B. stop operating. C. use more diesel.

full.text: During the first phase of the trial, sensors were placed along a river to record water levels. After heavy rain, the data helped researchers identify sections at risk of flooding. The team later shared its findings with local officials, who used them to revise emergency response maps.

Match beginnings 1–3 with endings A–D.1. The sensors were positioned along the river to ...2. After heavy rain, the data allowed researchers to ...3. Local officials used the results to ...A. improve emergency planning maps.B. identify locations at risk of flooding.C. monitor changes in water level.D. prevent all future floods.

rows: Record water levels = monitor their changes.
Identify sections at risk of flooding.

Use FALSE only if the passage contradicts the statement; otherwise consider NOT GIVEN.
